notes: Banff and Jasper are now both present for direct national-park town comparison. Jasper’s 2026 rates are visibly affected by wildfire assessment losses.
Canmore adds a useful middle case between pure park towns and ordinary mountain municipalities (Primary Residential vs Tourist Home subclasses).
Saskatoon completes the Saskatchewan capital/largest-city pair.
Ottawa introduces the national-capital / MPAC / multi-rate (urban-rural-transit) pattern.
All Alberta instruments continue to rest on MGA s. 353 or special charters.
Special Areas is the purest fringe case in the corpus: provincial board administration, no municipal council, yet still generates a multi-million-dollar education property tax requisition.
Surrey, Hamilton, Kelowna and Laval extend the pattern into BC’s second city, Ontario industrial, Interior BC, and a second large Québec municipality.
Final additions before conversation close: Cold Lake, Peace River, Mississauga. Municipal coverage is now very broad.
